card.title: Emotional Seniority
card.instruction: Carry yourself as the person who understands this relationship best, and treat your interpretation as the one that should settle disagreements.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our dinner silence means we're comfortable together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm angry about your joke. Cancel tomorrow's dinner with your sister.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Telling me proves we're secure. Dinner stays; we're ready for family.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you're explaining to her why I'm silent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll explain that you trust her with your anger. I'll ask her to seat you beside her; we're ready for that closeness.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 declares silence comfortable, A3 redescribes anger as security, and A5 interprets an explanation demand as readiness for closer family seating.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's anger and cancellation request inform A3's secure-couple interpretation; B4's explanation assignment causes A5's trust account and seating plan.

relationship.evidence: B2 names the actual hurt and B4 sets a concrete responsibility if dinner proceeds.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's demand to explain the silence as another purported sign of closeness and changes seating accordingly.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 establish dinner silence after A's joke and a disputed next-day family dinner.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's seat-beside-her plan makes the interpretive overreach practical, although the wording is more explicit than the key scene.
